Jane S: Hey team — customer asks if we can ship a minimal egress exception for their offline POC. They want to avoid full internet access but allow a single proxied outbound to fetch signed bundles.
Miguel R: short answer: yes, with caveats. need firewall allowlist + strict SNI + cert pinning on the proxy.
Amy L: what exactly does their infra want to allow? IPs, FQDNs, ports?
Tom K: they can only open one outbound to a corporate proxy on TCP/443. No DNS whitelisting allowed on their side.
Jane S: okay so they'd like a single FQDN that resolves internally and then we push signed bundle via that proxy. pricing question: does this change POC scope?
Amy L: it does a bit — we'll need to produce an encrypted chunked offline bundle and sign each chunk. Adds ~2 engineer-days for packaging + infra to support proxy flow.
Miguel R: operational notes: bundle size < 1.5GB recommended for proxy timeouts. We recommend chunked deltas for upgrades. Also we need to TTL sign and include CRL/OCSP handling for cert rotation.
Jane S: security asks in questionnaire: how do we prove integrity on a constrained egress path?
sec-bot: Checklist: 1) Signed artifact SHA256 manifest 2) Timestamped signature (RFC 3161) 3) Reproducible build metadata 4) Public key fingerprint exchange via customer KMS/HSM or secure OOB.
Tom K: customer prefers using their HSM. Can we accept a customer-managed verification key instead of shipping ours?
Miguel R: yes — we can support customer-provided verification key. We'll provide a small script to import the pubkey into the installer. Documented command: ```./install --import-verifier /etc/redwood/verifier.pem```
Amy L: upgrade cadence: recommend quarterly security patches for POC but monthly delta patches if they want fast fixes. With chunked deltas upgrades can be staged via our offline bundle tool.
Jane S: any blockers for licensing or support tiers here?
Tom K: for access to signed bundles and on-prem packaging we need an enterprise SOW (one-off packaging fee + 12mo support). I'll flag pricing: $8k packaging + $2k/mo for retention + support.
Miguel R: note on proxy: we need SNI passthrough so we can verify TLS peername; if customer intercepts TLS we fall back to signed-bundle verification but that requires timestamping. If they do MITM, we need the verifier key OOB.
Jane S: action items: Miguel — document exact firewall/proxy requirements and sample curl to validate. Amy — estimate engineering days and write the packaging SOW blurb. Tom — send pricing and contract template to customer. sec-bot — attach checklist to questionnaire response.
Amy L: I can have a short POC-runbook draft by EOD tomorrow.
Miguel R: I'll paste the minimal allowlist and a test command: ```# allowlist: outbound to proxy fqdn: proxy.corp.example on :443; curl --proxy https://proxy.corp.example:443 -I https://packages.redwood.io/signed-bundle-v1.tar.gz```
Tom K: pinging @customer for signoff on proxy approach.
Jane S: thanks all :thumbsup: — keeping notes here for the deal thread.
